records.referenced_statement: Demailly Paun 2004 Theorem 3.2: Let alpha be any smooth real (1,1)-form on a compact Hermitian manifold and let u be alpha-plurisubharmonic. There are delta_j decreasing to 0 and u_j in PSH(X,alpha+delta_j omega) decreasing to u, smooth off analytic pole sets, and after finite sequences of blowups with smooth centers pi_j^*u_j=sum_l a_l log|s_l|+b with a_l>0 and b smooth; normal crossing divisors. Apply to the closed current dd^c u with arbitrary smooth lower bound -alpha, not assumed closed.

records.context_expansion: The theorem concerns a closed current T=A+i∂∂bar psi on a compact complex manifold equipped with a Hermitian metric. Its smooth lower bound gamma is not required to be closed. Items (i)-(iii) give smoothness off analytic sets, vanishing curvature error, and decreasing potentials. Item (iv) explicitly gives blowups with smooth centers, normal crossing divisors, positive integral multiplicities times a positive scale, and smooth local remainders.
records.application_check: Set the theorem's smooth part A=0, psi=u (rescaling for the fixed dd^c convention), and gamma=-alpha. Then T=dd^c u is closed even for nonclosed alpha. The lower-bound estimate becomes dd^c u_j >= -alpha-delta_j omega. The positive multiplicities and normalization constants yield the submitted positive logarithmic coefficients. Further principalization yields simple normal crossings if needed. No additional multiplier-ideal sequence properties are imported. Strict rho follows by applying the same theorem to an initially strict potential with error smaller than its strict lower bound.

records.referenced_statement: BGL25 published Section 4 Theorems 4.6 and 4.7: For every smooth big real (1,1)-form theta on a compact Hermitian manifold, every nonzero nonnegative f in L^p with p>1, and every lambda>0, there exists a unique theta-plurisubharmonic potential u with ordinary minimal singularities u equivalent to V_theta satisfying MA_theta(u)=e^{lambda u} f dV. There exist a theta-plurisubharmonic potential v with ordinary minimal singularities and sup_X v=0 and a unique c>0 satisfying MA_theta(v)=c f dV; uniqueness of the normalized potential is not asserted.

No PVP premise is introduced. Theorem 4.6 gives ordinary minimal type V_theta+O(1), existence and uniqueness for each positive exponent. Theorem 4.7 gives V_theta-C<=phi<=V_theta and a unique positive scalar; potential uniqueness is not asserted.
